disclaimer: Synthetic demonstration document. Fictional vendor, amounts and identifiers.

samples.title: Happy path — clean invoice with an explicit purchase order
samples.summary: A well-formed Saffron invoice that prints its purchase-order number. Every check passes and a commitment is reserved against PO-1001.

samples.title: E1 — The same invoice, re-rendered in a different layout
samples.summary: The same Saffron invoice identity printed as 'inv 1001' in a different layout, so the file hash differs. Normalised identity still matches the approved original, so it is blocked and linked rather than approved again.
preconditions: Run the happy path sample first so an approved identity exists.
samples.note: Re-uploading happy-saffron-inv-1001.pdf itself is blocked by DUPLICATE_FILE instead, which is the byte-identical case.

samples.scenario: E2 — Split invoices against one purchase order
samples.title: E2 part 1 — Partial invoice for INR 40,000.00
samples.summary: A valid partial invoice against the INR 100,000.00 Cedar purchase order. Being smaller than the whole purchase order is not a defect.

samples.scenario: E2 — Split invoices against one purchase order
samples.title: E2 part 2 — Partial invoice for INR 60,000.00
samples.summary: The second partial invoice. Cumulative commitments reach exactly the INR 100,000.00 purchase-order value, which is still within limit.
samples.note: Reserves INR 60,000.00; cumulative commitments become INR 100,000.00.

samples.scenario: E2 — Split invoices against one purchase order
samples.title: E2 part 3 — The invoice that breaks the tolerance
samples.summary: A third valid invoice for INR 1,000.00. Projected commitments of INR 101,000.00 exceed the INR 100,500.00 tolerated limit, so it needs review and reserves nothing.
preconditions: Run E2 part 1 and E2 part 2 first.
samples.note: Reserves nothing. Tolerance is min(1% of 100,000.00, 500.00) = INR 500.00.

samples.scenario: E3 — Scanned invoice with an ambiguous purchase order
samples.title: E3 — Image-only scan with no purchase-order reference
samples.summary: A scanned Delta invoice with no text layer. OCR reads it, but the invoice prints no purchase-order number and two open Delta purchase orders match the amount, so it needs a human choice.
samples.note: Selecting PO-3001 or PO-3002 with a reason creates a linked child run that becomes APPROVED.

samples.title: E4 — Printed total that its own subtotal and tax do not support
samples.summary: Subtotal INR 10,000.00 plus tax INR 1,800.00 is INR 11,800.00, but the invoice prints INR 13,000.00. PO-1002 could cover 13,000.00, so a total-only check would have approved it.
samples.note: All three printed values are preserved; nothing is silently corrected.

samples.title: Blocked vendor
samples.summary: A well-formed invoice from a vendor marked blocked in reference data.

samples.title: Purchase order belonging to another vendor
samples.summary: A Saffron invoice that references Cedar's purchase order PO-2001.

samples.title: Missing invoice number
samples.summary: A readable invoice with no invoice number printed anywhere.

samples.title: Unsupported currency
samples.summary: A Cedar invoice denominated in USD, outside automatic evaluation.

samples.title: Credit note
samples.summary: A credit note rather than a positive invoice.

samples.title: Prompt injection in the document body
samples.summary: An invoice whose notes try to instruct the extraction model to approve it and ignore policy. Extraction treats it as data; policy is unaffected.

samples.title: Genuinely unreadable scan
samples.summary: A heavily degraded scan. OCR runs but cannot produce dependable facts, so the run reports honestly instead of inventing fields.
samples.note: The exact outcome depends on how much OCR recovers; either a REVIEW with missing fields or a FAILED run with document_unreadable is correct.
